title: The earliest high-fired glazed ceramics in China: Scientific studies of the proto-porcelain from Zhejiang during the Shang and Zhou periods (c. 1700 – 221 BC)

passages.quote: began to appear in China during the Shang dynasty (c. 1700 to 1027 BC)

passages.note: Reports analytical interpretation of deliberately applied lime-rich wood ash on sampled Deqing proto-porcelain, and local porcelain stone for bodies.
Lists 12 excavated Nanshan sherds and one kiln wall as Shang, and distinguishes other Deqing sites and periods.

passages.locator: pp. 132–135 and 138–143; Appendix 3, Table A 3.1, p. 271
passages.note: Interprets vessel glaze as lime-rich surface material interacting with body during firing, contrasts kiln wall vitrification, and cannot decide between washed ash and potash-depleted firebox ash. Glaze analyses are tabulated for four Nanshan sherds NS-1, NS-4, NS-8 and NS-11.
